question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $g(x,y)h(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x,y) & =3{x}^{2}-4y,\, &  & ∇g(x,y)=6x\text{ }i-4\text{ }j, &  &  \\ h(x,y) & =2{x}^{2}{y}^{2},\, &  & ∇h(x,y)=4x{y}^{2}\text{ }i+4{x}^{2}y\text{ }j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $g(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[gh]=h\,∇\,g+g\,∇\,h
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[g(x,y)h(x,y)] & =h(x,y)∇g(x,y)+g(x,y)∇h(x,y) \\  & =2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}(6x\text{ }i-4\text{ }j)+(3{x}^{2}-4y)(4x{y}^{2}\text{ }i+4{x}^{2}y\text{ }j) \\  & =(2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\cdot 6x\text{ }i-2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\cdot 4\text{ }j)+((3{x}^{2}-4y)\cdot 4x{y}^{2}\text{ }i+(3{x}^{2}-4y)\cdot 4{x}^{2}y\text{ }j) \\  & =12{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\text{ }i-8{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }j+(12{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-16x{y}^{3})\text{ }i+(12{x}^{4}y-16{x}^{2}{y}^{2})\text{ }j \\  & =(24{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-16x{y}^{3})\text{ }i+(12{x}^{4}y-24{x}^{2}{y}^{2})\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}$ and $g(x,y)={e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=f∇g+g∇f.
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2})={y}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2})=2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={y}^{2}\text{ }i+2xy\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})})=-2x{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})})=-2y{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}\text{ }j=-2x{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }i-2y{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =x{y}^{2}(-2x{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }i-2y{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }j)+{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}({y}^{2}\text{ }i+2xy\text{ }j) \\  & ={e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}(-2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }i-2x{y}^{3}\text{ }j)+{e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}({y}^{2}\text{ }i+2xy\text{ }j) \\  & ={e}^{-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}({y}^{2}(1-2{x}^{2})\text{ }i+2xy(1-{y}^{2})\text{ }j).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y,z)h(x,y,z),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =x{y}^{2}{z}^{3},\, &  & ∇f(x,y,z)={y}^{2}{z}^{3}\,i+2xy{z}^{3}\,j+3x{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,k, &  &  \\ h(x,y,z) & =\frac{1}{xyz},\, &  & ∇h(x,y,z)=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}yz}\,i-\frac{1}{x{y}^{2}z}\,j-\frac{1}{xy{z}^{2}}\text{ }k. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fh]=h∇f+f∇h.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y,z)h(x,y,z)] & =h(x,y,z)∇f(x,y,z)+f(x,y,z)∇h(x,y,z) \\  & =\frac{1}{xyz}({y}^{2}{z}^{3}\,i+2xy{z}^{3}\,j+3x{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,k)+x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}yz}\,i-\frac{1}{x{y}^{2}z}\,j-\frac{1}{xy{z}^{2}}\,k) \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}{z}^{3}}{xyz}\,i+\frac{2xy{z}^{3}}{xyz}\,j+\frac{3x{y}^{2}{z}^{2}}{xyz}\,k-\frac{x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}}{{x}^{2}yz}\,i-\frac{x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}z}\,j-\frac{x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}}{xy{z}^{2}}\,k \\  & =\frac{y{z}^{2}}{x}\,i+2{z}^{2}\,j+3yz\,k-\frac{y{z}^{2}}{x}\,i-{z}^{2}\,j-yz\,k \\  & ={z}^{2}\,j+2yz\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =xy,\, &  & ∇f(x,y)=y\text{ }i+x\text{ }j, &  &  \\ g(x,y) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy),\, &  & ∇g(x,y)=\frac{1}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fg]=g\,∇\,f+f\,∇\,g
$$

So, using this product rule we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))(y\text{ }i+x\text{ }j)+xy(\frac{1}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j) \\  & =y\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)\text{ }i+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)\text{ }j+y\text{ }i+x\text{ }j \\  & =[y\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)\text{ }i+y\text{ }i]+[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)\text{ }j+x\text{ }j] \\  & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+1)\text{ }i+x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+1)\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2},\, &  & ∇f(x,y)=(2xy+{y}^{2})\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+2xy)\text{ }j, &  &  \\ h(x,y) & =\frac{1}{xy},\, &  & ∇h(x,y)=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}y}\text{ }i-\frac{1}{x{y}^{2}}\text{ }j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=h\,∇\,f+f\,∇\,h
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =h(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇h(x,y) \\  & =\frac{1}{xy}((2xy+{y}^{2})\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+2xy)\text{ }j)+({x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}y}\text{ }i-\frac{1}{x{y}^{2}}\text{ }j) \\  & =(\frac{2xy+{y}^{2}}{xy}\text{ }i+\frac{{x}^{2}+2xy}{xy}\text{ }j)+(-\frac{{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}y}\text{ }i-\frac{{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2}}{x{y}^{2}}\text{ }j) \\  & =(\frac{2x+y}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{x+2y}{y}\text{ }j)+(-\frac{x+y}{x}\text{ }i-\frac{x+y}{y}\text{ }j) \\  & =(-\frac{x+y}{x}+\frac{2x+y}{x})\text{ }i+(-\frac{x+y}{y}+\frac{x+2y}{y})\text{ }j \\  & =\text{ }i+\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $g(x,y)h(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x,y) & ={e}^{x-y},\, &  & ∇g(x,y)={e}^{x-y}\,i-{e}^{x-y}\,j, &  &  \\ h(x,y) & ={x}^{2}-3xy,\, &  & ∇h(x,y)=(2x-3y)\,i-3x\,j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $g(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[gh]=h∇g+g∇h.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[g(x,y)h(x,y)] & =h(x,y)∇g(x,y)+g(x,y)∇h(x,y) \\  & =({x}^{2}-3xy)({e}^{x-y}\,i-{e}^{x-y}\,j)+{e}^{x-y}((2x-3y)\,i-3x\,j) \\  & =(({x}^{2}-3xy){e}^{x-y}\,i-({x}^{2}-3xy){e}^{x-y}\,j)+((2x-3y){e}^{x-y}\,i-3x{e}^{x-y}\,j) \\  & ={e}^{x-y}({x}^{2}-3xy+2x-3y)\,i-{e}^{x-y}({x}^{2}-3xy+3x)\,j \\  & ={e}^{x-y}(({x}^{2}-3xy+2x-3y)\,i-({x}^{2}-3xy+3x)\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $g(x,y)h(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x,y) & ={e}^{xy},\, &  & ∇g(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}\text{ }i+x{e}^{xy}\text{ }j, &  &  \\ h(x,y) & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2},\, &  & ∇h(x,y)=2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $g(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[gh]=h\,∇\,g+g\,∇\,h
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[g(x,y)h(x,y)] & =h(x,y)∇g(x,y)+g(x,y)∇h(x,y) \\  & =({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})(y{e}^{xy}\text{ }i+x{e}^{xy}\text{ }j)+{e}^{xy}(2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j) \\  & =(({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})y{e}^{xy}\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})x{e}^{xy}\text{ }j)+(2x{e}^{xy}\text{ }i+2y{e}^{xy}\text{ }j) \\  & =({x}^{2}y+{y}^{3}+2x){e}^{xy}\text{ }i+({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+2y){e}^{xy}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y}$ and $h(x,y)=y{e}^{x}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=f\,∇\,h+h\,∇\,f\,\,
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y})={e}^{y} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y})=x{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{y}\text{ }i+x{e}^{y}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{x})=y{e}^{x} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})={e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y) & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\text{ }j=y{e}^{x}\text{ }i+{e}^{x}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =x{e}^{y}(y{e}^{x}\text{ }i+{e}^{x}\text{ }j)+y{e}^{x}({e}^{y}\text{ }i+x{e}^{y}\text{ }j) \\  & =xy{e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+x{e}^{x+y}\text{ }j+y{e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+xy{e}^{x+y}\text{ }j \\  & =(x+1)y{e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+x(1+y){e}^{x+y}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =4 x + 3 y,\quad ∇f(x,y)=(4)\,i+(3)\,j \\ g(x,y) & =4 x - 2 y,\quad ∇g(x,y)=(4)\,i+(-2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(4 x - 2 y)((4)\,i+(3)\,j)+(4 x + 3 y)((4)\,i+(-2)\,j) \\  & =(4 x - 2 y)(4)i+(4 x - 2 y)(3)j+(4 x + 3 y)(4)i+(4 x + 3 y)(-2)j \\  & =(16 x - 8 y)i+(12 x - 6 y)j+(16 x + 12 y)i+(- 8 x - 6 y)j \\  & =(32 x + 4 y)\,i+(4 x - 12 y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}$ and $h(x,y)=(y+4){e}^{(x-3)}?$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: (- \left(x - 3\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4} + \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4})\,i+(\left(x - 3\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4} - \left(x - 3\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4})\,j

question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=f\,∇\,h+h\,∇\,f\,\,
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-3){e}^{(y+4)})={e}^{(y+4)} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-3){e}^{(y+4)})=(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)})=(y+4){e}^{(x-3)} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)})={e}^{(x-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y) & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\text{ }j=(y+4){e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }j)+(y+4){e}^{(x-3)}({e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j) \\  & =(x-3)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j+(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j \\  & =((x-3)+1)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3)(1+(y+4)){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z),$ given that $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3}$ and $g(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{x y z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y,z)$ and $g(x,y,z)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}k=(2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})\,i+(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})\,j+(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $g(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}j+\frac{∂g}{∂z}k=(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z)] & =g(x,y,z)∇f(x,y,z)+f(x,y,z)∇g(x,y,z) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})((2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})\,i+(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})\,j+(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})\,k)+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})((- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})(2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})i+(\frac{1}{x y z})(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})j+(\frac{1}{x y z})(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})k+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})i+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})j+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})k \\  & =(2 y^{2} - \frac{z^{2}}{x})i+(3 x y - \frac{z^{2}}{y})j+(\frac{x y^{2}}{z} - 3 z)k+(- y^{2} + \frac{z^{2}}{x})i+(- x y + \frac{z^{2}}{y})j+(- \frac{x y^{2}}{z} + z)k \\  & =(y^{2})\,i+(2 x y)\,j+(- 2 z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =- 2 x + 2 y,\quad ∇f(x,y)=(-2)\,i+(2)\,j \\ g(x,y) & =- x - y,\quad ∇g(x,y)=(-1)\,i+(-1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(- x - y)((-2)\,i+(2)\,j)+(- 2 x + 2 y)((-1)\,i+(-1)\,j) \\  & =(- x - y)(-2)i+(- x - y)(2)j+(- 2 x + 2 y)(-1)i+(- 2 x + 2 y)(-1)j \\  & =(2 x + 2 y)i+(- 2 x - 2 y)j+(2 x - 2 y)i+(2 x - 2 y)j \\  & =(4 x)\,i+(- 4 y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}$ and $h(x,y)=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}?$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: (- \left(x + 1\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4} + \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4})\,i+(\left(x + 1\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4} - \left(x + 1\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4})\,j

question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=f\,∇\,h+h\,∇\,f\,\,
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+1){e}^{(y+4)})={e}^{(y+4)} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x+1){e}^{(y+4)})=(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)})=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)})={e}^{(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y) & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\text{ }j=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }j)+(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}({e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j) \\  & =(x+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j+(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j \\  & =((x+1)+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1)(1+(y+4)){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$
